Every level reaches 75 lessons. A lesson is one station step run under one condition; each level's number is its tasks' steps added up from the station modules.

The ladder

Level 1 is open; each level opens when the one below is passed — every task in one run of it a mastery run. A task opens its station with its condition; the number after each task is its steps.

Track Access

12 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 3.7 min

Roadway-worker protection: the authority, the watchman and the clear time before the rail is occupied.

  • union — BMWED roadway worker training for track and structures maintenance
  • FRA — 49 CFR Part 214 — Railroad workplace safety, including roadway worker protection
  • union — SMART and the International Training Institute — sheet metal, rail and transportation apprenticeship

Wheelchair Lift & Securement on a Bus

14 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5.3 min · indoors

The stop that makes the route accessible: the boarding pad checked clear, all four securement points locked and tensioned, and the lift watched clean back into its stow before the bus moves.

  • DOJ — Americans with Disabilities Act Title II — programme accessibility for public entities and their services
  • union — ATU member training for bus and rail transit operations
  • FTA — FTA guidance implementing the Department of Transportation's ADA rules for wheelchair lifts, ramps and securement on fixed-route transit buses
  • union — IBEW/NECA Joint Apprenticeship and Training Committee — inside and outside wireman apprenticeship standards, taught from the electrical training ALLIANCE curriculum
  • NEC/NFPA 70 — NFPA 70 — National Electrical Code

What it proves

Competency: Take access and move equipment on live rail and airfield operations

Demonstrated with a mastery run on 4 of its 7 stations, against FRA 49 CFR 214 Subpart C Roadway worker protection; FAA 14 CFR 139 Certification of airports; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178 Powered industrial trucks.

Badges

Each passed level earns an Open Badges 2.0 assertion naming the level, its tasks and their conditions, its lessons and the standards it evidences, with the attempts behind it as evidence, and sends an xAPI statement. Passing level 20, the capstone, climbs the whole track.

A run demonstrates mastery when it earns two or more stars, records zero unsafe actions, answers every interruption it was given, and finishes within 1.5 times the station's par time. One mastery run on enough of a competency's stations earns "demonstrated"; mastery runs on three different days earn "consistent". No other rule earns a competency.

Certification the work leads to: FRA roadway-worker protection, FTA rail transit safety practice, FAA 14 CFR 139 airfield operations and OSHA 1910.178 for powered equipment. No level claims apprenticeship hours: no registry entry states an equivalence.

Generated from the programme's station modules: lesson counts are read, not typed. The rules are in tools/briefs/ladder-brief.md and the full table in docs/ladders.md.
